title: I went to the shop to ...
subtitle: to ... = why
summary: Use to + verb to say why somebody does something, use for + noun for the thing itself, and learn wait for / wait to.

lesson.heading: Why did she go?
lesson.text: Paula wanted a newspaper, so she went to the shop. Why did she go to the shop? **To get** a newspaper. We use **to** + verb to say *why* a person does something.

examples.text: *A:* Why are you going out? *B:* **To get** some bread.
Catherine went to the station **to meet** her friend.
Sue turned on the television **to watch** the news.
I'd like to go to Spain **to learn** Spanish.

lesson.heading: money to ... / time to ...
lesson.text: We also use **to** + verb after *money* and *time* to say what the money or the time is for.

examples.text: We need some **money to buy** food.
I haven't got **time to watch** television.

lesson.heading: to ... and for ...

left.label: to + verb (to get / to see)
examples: I went to the shop **to get** a newspaper.
They're going to Brazil **to see** their friends.
We need some money **to buy** food.

right.label: for + noun (for a newspaper / for food)
examples: I went to the shop **for a newspaper**.
They're going to Brazil **for a holiday**.

lesson.note: We say *to get a newspaper*, not ~~for get a newspaper~~.

lesson.heading: wait for ... and wait to ...
lesson.text: Use **wait for** + a person or thing. Use **wait to** + verb when you say what you want to do.

examples.text: Are you **waiting to** see the doctor?

lesson.heading: wait for somebody to ...
lesson.text: Sometimes you wait for another person to do something. Then we say **wait for** + somebody + **to** + verb. A woman is sitting by the phone. She says she can't go out yet.

examples.text: I can't go out yet. I'm **waiting for John to phone**.
Are you **waiting for the doctor to come**?

lesson.text: A verb after the reason takes **to**: *I went out to buy bread*. A noun takes **for**: *I went out for some bread*.

exercises.prompt: Paula wanted a newspaper. She went to the shop ___ a newspaper.
exercises.explanation: We use to + verb to say why: She went to the shop to get a newspaper.

exercises.prompt: 'Why are you going out?' '___ some bread.'
exercises.explanation: The answer to Why ... ? can be to + verb: To get some bread.

exercises.prompt: Match the place with the reason for going there.

pairs.left: I went to the post office

exercises.prompt: We went to a restaurant ___ have dinner.
exercises.explanation: A verb (have) comes after it, so we use to.

exercises.prompt: I'm going to London ___ an interview next week.
exercises.explanation: A noun (an interview) comes after it, so we use for.
money to + verb: money to live.

exercises.prompt: We didn't have any money ___ a taxi, so we walked home.
exercises.explanation: money for + noun: money for a taxi.

exercises.prompt: Do these words come after to or after for?

exercises.statement: I went to the shop for get a newspaper.
exercises.explanation: Before a verb we use to: I went to the shop to get a newspaper.

exercises.prompt: Alice sat down in an armchair ___ the newspaper.
exercises.explanation: to + verb gives the reason: to read the newspaper.

exercises.prompt: The doorbell rang, so I looked out of the window ___ who it was.
exercises.explanation: to + verb gives the reason: to see who it was.

exercises.prompt: I can't go out yet. I'm waiting ___ to phone.
exercises.explanation: wait for + somebody + to ...: I'm waiting for John to phone.

exercises.prompt: You are in the cinema before the film. Put the sentence in order.
exercises.answer: I sat down in the cinema and waited for the film to begin.
exercises.explanation: wait for + something + to ...: waited for the film to begin.
